items.label: Industry: Critical Minerals & Precious Metals Mining
items.detail: Selected from active-conviction account holdings: with NVDA and DELL fully exited, the account's largest single-theme cluster is now CCJ, FCX, KGC, NEM, REMX, IGLN, and SSLV (~$85.0k, 17.4% of NAV) spanning uranium, copper, gold, silver, and rare earths, each running a structural multi-year supply deficit (copper 150k-600k t in 2026 alone; silver's 6th straight annual deficit; uranium mined supply covering <75% of reactor demand) except gold, which is investment-driven and currently the hottest M&A subsector in the cluster.

items.label: CCJ
items.detail: Existing holding, thesis reinforced: spot uranium eased to ~$85.80/lb (Apr 2026) after topping $100/lb in January, but the deficit keeps widening -- a majority of surveyed investors expect mined uranium to cover under 75% of future reactor demand, and Sprott models a cumulative 197M-lb shortfall by 2040.
items.diversification_note: Already the account's entire IBKR 'Energy' sector bucket (2.02% of NAV, $9,869) -- adding to this position increases concentration in a sector that is already the account's uranium sleeve, not a diversifier.

items.label: FCX
items.detail: Existing holding, thesis reinforced: the 2026 refined copper deficit (analyst range 150,000-600,000 tonnes) is on track to be the largest in 20+ years, and Freeport's own Grasberg restart slipping from 2027 to 2028 tightens supply further even as it caps Freeport's own near-term volume growth.
items.diversification_note: Part of the account's 'Basic Materials' sector bucket (5.32% of NAV, $26,049 combined with KGC/NEM/REMX) -- adding here increases concentration in an already-large materials/metals sleeve.

items.label: KGC / NEM
items.detail: Existing holdings, watch only: gold is the most active M&A subsector in this cluster right now -- Equinox Gold/Orla Mining ($5.13B deal, ~$18.5B combined), Agnico Eagle's 3-deal Lapland roll-up (~$2.8B), and Goldgroup/Gold Resource ($372M) all closed or announced in 2026. Neither has a confirmed catalyst; flagging the subsector's heat, not a specific action.
items.diversification_note: Both sit in the same 'Basic Materials' bucket as FCX/REMX (5.32% of NAV combined) -- gold's investment/rate-driven demand is a different risk factor than copper/uranium's physical-shortage driver, so the pair is a partial macro diversifier within an otherwise concentrated sleeve.

items.label: UUUU
items.detail: Energy Fuels -- not currently held. Largest US conventional uranium producer and simultaneously the first US company producing heavy rare earth oxides (dysprosium, terbium) at meaningful purity from domestic ore, via its licensed White Mesa Mill -- a dual thesis on the uranium deficit already in the account (CCJ) plus the separate heavy-REE reshoring theme. Last price $14.60.
items.diversification_note: Would sit alongside CCJ in the 'Energy' sector bucket -- adds to existing uranium exposure, but its heavy-REE segment is a genuinely new leg not represented elsewhere in the account except via the diversified REMX ETF.
items.suggested_size: Starter/scout position, roughly 0.5-1% of account NAV (~$2,500-$5,000); heavy-REE output is still early-stage (tens of kg) and unproven at industrial scale.

items.label: HBM
items.detail: Hudbay Minerals -- not currently held. Active copper-gold-zinc consolidator in the Americas (just acquired Arizona Sonoran for ~$1.48B at a 30% premium), a differentiated way to play the copper deficit versus the account's existing FCX (a major, not a consolidator). Last price $28.55.
items.diversification_note: Would land in the account's 'Basic Materials' bucket alongside FCX (5.32% of NAV combined with KGC/NEM/REMX) -- adds a second copper name and increases single-commodity concentration, though its consolidator profile differs from FCX's major-producer profile.
items.suggested_size: Starter/scout position, roughly 0.5-1% of account NAV (~$2,500-$5,000) given integration risk on its recent and pending acquisitions.

items.label: ARA
items.detail: Aclara Resources -- not currently held. Heavy rare earth (dysprosium/terbium) pure-play developer targeting over 75% of US Dy/Tb demand once its Penco, Carina, and Vinton facilities operate together -- direct single-name exposure to the DOD-backed magnet-reshoring theme the account currently only holds via the diversified REMX ETF. Last price C$3.90 (TSE).
items.diversification_note: Would land in 'Basic Materials' alongside REMX, but as the account's first single-name rare earth equity (vs. REMX's diversified basket) it is a genuine within-theme diversifier.
items.suggested_size: Smallest scout tranche of the group, roughly 0.25-0.5% of account NAV (~$1,250-$2,500), given its pre-revenue/early development stage and multi-facility execution risk.

items.label: PAAS
items.detail: Pan American Silver -- not currently held. Operating silver (plus gold byproduct) miner across a diversified Americas portfolio, giving direct operating leverage to the structural silver deficit (6th consecutive annual shortfall in 2026) that the account's existing SSLV position, a physical-tracking ETF, cannot provide. Last price $51.47.
items.diversification_note: Would be the account's first operating silver-mining equity -- distinct from SSLV (passive metal exposure) and from the gold miners (KGC/NEM), adding a fourth, structurally different leg to the precious-metals sleeve.
items.suggested_size: Starter/scout position, roughly 0.5-1% of account NAV (~$2,500-$5,000); UBS projects the 2026 silver deficit to narrow versus prior years, a near-term headwind to monitor.

items.label: Silver/copper royalty & streaming vehicles
items.detail: Technology/portfolio adoption gap flagged for further research: royalty and streaming companies offer leveraged, lower-operating-risk exposure to the same silver and copper deficits without mine-execution risk; no specific name meets scale/quality bar yet -- carry to next scout cycle.
